title: Google native trigger template flow

gaps.fragment: let pageToken: string | undefined = startPageToken; while (pageToken) { ... pageToken = data.nextPageToken; }
gaps.why: unbounded pagination loop over the Drive changes API; L0 refuses an unbounded while, pagination is an L3 binding capability with a page cap (L0 card note)

gaps.fragment: const state = await wmill.getState(); ... await wmill.setState({ startPageToken: data.newStartPageToken });
gaps.why: cross-run cursor plus a per-calendar sync token under one key map; L0 state (27) is designed not built, one writer per key holds

note: One-module flow: a Google Drive/Calendar push notification is routed by resource_uri (L0 if) to one of three handlers that call Google APIs and keep an incremental-sync cursor in flow state. Effects sit inside the script body, which becomes effect nodes in the rewrite. Not a refusal.

title: MQTT flow with preprocessor template
note: Template stub: flow body modules [] and only a trigger preprocessor that base64-decodes an MQTT payload and throws on any other trigger kind (L0 guard). The MQTT subscription is the trigger (trigger.event; a topic consumer is also P44's shape but nothing here batches).

title: Email trigger flow with preprocessor template
note: Template stub: empty flow body, a preprocessor that passes parsed_email/raw_email/extra args through and throws on another trigger kind. Inbound email is trigger.event.

title: Upon new user signup, check postgres, hash password, add to postgres and airtable, email

gaps.fragment: type forloopflow, skip_failures: true, iterator: result
gaps.why: for-each with skip_failures: a per-item failure policy (continue past a failed item); L0 map is fail-fast, so the rewrite puts a try/catch (P28 flagged fallback) inside the item function

gaps.fragment: const check_user_query = `SELECT user_id FROM usr WHERE email='${email}'`;
gaps.why: untrusted input concatenated into SQL; not a vocabulary gap, a latent defect the L3 binding (parameterised query) removes

note: A signup call: an existence check with an early-stop (stop_after_if, L0 if then done), then per item hash password, insert into Postgres, create an Airtable record and send a welcome mail via hub scripts (effects with L3 bindings). The loop runs over a list that always has one element. No wait, no model.

title: Send a message on discord if an endpoint is down

gaps.fragment: type forloopflow, parallel: false, skip_failures: true, iterator: flow_input.endpoints
gaps.why: sequential for-each that skips failed items (an unreachable endpoint must not stop the loop); per-item failure policy is not an L0 map field

note: For each endpoint: HTTP status check (effect), a branchone on status != 200 (guard before an effect), then a Discord webhook message. No trigger declared in the definition (a Windmill schedule would supply P36, which is not in this item). No reduce.

title: Do sentiment analysis on recent HackerNews mentions

gaps.fragment: Classify the sentiment in these mentions: ${results.d.map((m, i) => `${i}. ...`)} Sentiment ratings:
gaps.why: one judge returns a free-text list for a batch that code splits by line and aligns by position; the vocabulary's rule is one decision per judge with an id-echoing closed object, so the batch becomes a P13 map with an id echo; a rewrite, not a missing construct

note: A hub trigger script returns new HackerNews items matching phrases (poll with its own cursor, stop_after_if on empty), one OpenAI completion rates sentiment for the whole batch, and a code step zips mentions with ratings. Nothing is delivered in the flow. Model id is a literal (L3/policy).

title: SQS flow with preprocessor template
note: Template stub: empty flow body, a preprocessor that JSON-parses an SQS message body and throws on a parse failure or another trigger kind. Queue message as trigger.event (stream if batched; nothing here batches).

title: Form to Table

gaps.fragment: suspend: { timeout: 1800, required_events: 1, continue_on_disapprove_timeout: true } ... const { approvalPage, resume, cancel } = await wmill.getResumeUrls('Approve Link')
gaps.why: approval whose resume and cancel callback URLs are written into a table cell and answered by the approver in another system; L0 approve is a human node with an answer schema, the callback-URL transport and the timeout-continues rule are L3/envelope detail

gaps.fragment: results.form.filled_out
gaps.why: validation of PDF form fields in code before any effect (P08 guard); the incomplete case notifies the uploader

note: A PDF upload event: read the form (code), if every required field is filled then write a Nextcloud Tables row, attach file links, put an approval link in the row and suspend for 30 minutes for an approver; approved leads to a calendar entry, rejected or timed out to a status edit; an incomplete form sends a notification. Approval gate before an effect is P32 with an on-timeout route.

title: Reimbursement

gaps.fragment: Analyze Image (nextcloud) ... imageFileIds: [flow_input.iter.value.fileId], prompt: 'You are a precise data extraction assistant. Extract expense data ... respond ONLY with a valid CSV'
gaps.why: vision model reads receipt images and returns CSV text that code parses into a spreadsheet; a judge takes text; image inputs are not a field of L0 judge, so the read is an L3 tool call (analyze_image) and its CSV output is untrusted text to be validated

gaps.fragment: type forloopflow, parallel: true, skip_failures: true, iterator: answers.filter(files)
gaps.why: parallel for-each over receipts that skips failed items; per-item failure policy again

note: A form submission event: create a folder, then three parallel branches (per-receipt copy and vision extraction; trip dates; trip location) feed an XLSX filled by code, tagged, shared with the submitter and line manager (parallel for-each), then a notification. Extract, merge, deliver. No approval, no wait.

note: Template stub: empty flow body, a preprocessor that base64-decodes and JSON-parses a Kafka message (brokers, topic, group id in the event) and throws on a parse failure or another trigger kind. A Kafka topic subscription is the stream construct (30) with the P44 bounded consumer shape; no batching in this item.

title: Kafka Schema Registry compatibility and mode drift guard

gaps.fragment: type io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.Loop, concurrencyLimit: 1 ... row_save: kv.Set key audit_key value merged (an accumulator folded into the KV store once per iteration)
gaps.why: a sequential loop whose iterations fold into one external accumulator; the rewrite is a map with a typed reduce (no cross-iteration store, one writer)

gaps.fragment: type io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.Pause, onResume: [{id: approved, type: BOOL, required: false}] ... condition: outputs.approve.onResume.approved ?? false
gaps.why: human gate returning a typed answer that routes the remediation; L0 approve (16) with an answer schema and a reject/timeout route covers it

note: Audit every registry subject (two settings per subject) against a governed baseline, alert, and only with auto_remediate=true and dry_run=false pause for approval, PUT the drifted settings, re-read every targeted subject and fail the run if any is still off. Read effects, a per-subject loop, reconcile observed against baseline (P17 by hand), approval gate before writes (P32), verify-after-write, error route to Slack. Schedule shipped disabled. Needs no construct L0 lacks.

title: Sync Stripe payments and customers to a PostgreSQL CRM daily

gaps.fragment: upsert_to_postgres: python Script ... cur.execute('INSERT INTO crm_payments ... ON CONFLICT (payment_id) DO UPDATE ...')
gaps.why: the database write happens inside a code script; the vocabulary puts effects in envelope nodes, so the script is split into a step that builds rows and an effect with an idempotency key (P02 note)

note: Daily fetch of Stripe charges and customers, a Python merge and enrich, an idempotent upsert, a stored last-sync timestamp (KV Set; the Get result is read but not used, the window comes from the input) and a Slack summary. Fetch, transform, write with a cursor.

title: Guard PostgreSQL connection saturation with Slack alerts

gaps.fragment: triggers: every_5_minutes (Schedule) and on_demand_webhook (Webhook, key: secret('WEBHOOK_KEY'))
gaps.why: one workflow with two independent entry points; L0 has one input per solver, so each trigger is an envelope that calls the same solver (the earlier audits recorded this as 'several entry points')

note: Two SQL reads of pg_stat_activity, a Python severity calculation against warn and critical thresholds, an alert with top applications or a quiet log, an output of metrics and an error route to Slack. Scheduled and on-demand webhook starts share the body.

title: Run Mistral agent workflows from Kestra with completion polling

gaps.fragment: io.kestra.plugin.mistral.RunWorkflow ... wait: true, pollInterval: PT5S, waitTimeout: PT15M
gaps.why: a remote agent workflow is started and polled until terminal inside one plugin task; as an effect with a polling capability bound in L3 (P21 poll until ready, bounded by the timeout), the remote run is opaque to L0, which is the intended reading of an external agent as a tool

note: Start a registered Mistral workflow with two inputs, poll every 5 s for at most 15 minutes, post the terminal status to Slack; an error handler alerts on failure or timeout. The agent runs elsewhere; nothing here lets a model choose agents, tools or control flow. Not an agent-framework item in the refusal sense.

title: AWS CodeDeploy failed deployment sentinel

gaps.fragment: aws deploy list-deployments --application-name {{ inputs.application_name }} --deployment-group-name {{ inputs.deployment_group_name }} ... | tr -d '\n' | xargs -0 -I {} echo '::{"outputs":{}}::'
gaps.why: inputs are interpolated into a shell command line; a latent injection defect that the typed L3 binding (arguments, not a shell string) removes

note: List Failed deployments server-side, an if on a non-empty list fetches details and alerts Slack with ids and error codes, else logs healthy; a final log and an error route. Schedule shipped disabled.

title: Find GitHub Actions not pinned to a commit SHA

gaps.fragment: type io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.WorkingDirectory: tasks: [clone, find_unpinned] (clone and scan in the same working directory)
gaps.why: tasks share a mutable file workspace instead of a typed hand-off; the rewrite hands the checkout over as a typed artifact reference

gaps.fragment: urllib.request.Request(f'https://api.github.com/repos/{owner_repo}/commits/{ref}') ... inside resolve_shas python script
gaps.why: effects inside a code step (EFFECT_IN_SOLVER); split into effect nodes

note: Clone, scan workflow files for mutable action references (code), load the fingerprints already reported (KV), resolve each tag to its commit through the GitHub API, post only new findings to Slack, then store the current fingerprints (a seen-set, one writer). Poll, diff against stored state, notify.

title: Search GitHub org and log most starred repo
note: No trigger. Search an organization's repositories, convert Ion to JSON, log the first name. A three-task linear chain.

title: Scheduled sales analytics on CSV with DuckDB posted to Slack
note: Monday 09:00 schedule, one DuckDB query over a remote CSV (an effect with a SQL tool binding), one Slack message with two interpolated numbers.

title: Kestra flow failure rate gate
note: Hourly (shipped disabled): count failed and total executions of a namespace through the Kestra API, an if on the threshold alerts Slack with the rate or logs healthy, a final log, and an error route that alerts when the check itself fails. Read-only by design.

title: Stream Kestra audit logs from Kafka to BigQuery

gaps.fragment: io.kestra.plugin.kafka.Consume ... auto.offset.reset: earliest, maxRecords: 500
gaps.why: a bounded batch read of a topic inside a scheduled run; the consumer offset is state held by the broker, which L0 stream (30, bounded consumer) and state (27) express as a batch size and a cursor

note: Daily: consume up to 500 audit records from Kafka, a per-row JS transform, convert to Avro, load into BigQuery with WRITE_TRUNCATE (a destructive load without a gate; a defect, not a vocabulary gap).

title: Reserve stock for a new order

gaps.fragment: 'id': { 'S.$': 'States.UUID()' }
gaps.why: a fresh random identifier minted inside the definition; the vocabulary's step is pure code and has no randomness or clock, so the id is an input supplied by the host or an effect (the earlier audits recorded randomness and wall-clock time in a pure step as a gap)

gaps.fragment: Type: Parallel, Branches: [Update stock | Send stock reserved event | Write Item to InventoryReservationTable]
gaps.why: three effects run in parallel with no compensation if one fails; parallel effects are envelope fan-out (IR join), the saga (L0 compensate, N) would be the missing safety, which this definition does not have

note: Read a product's stock, a Choice on in-stock and enough stock; if yes a Parallel of three effects (decrement, event, reservation record), if no a Parallel of three notifications (purchase-order event, unavailable event, SNS). Guard before an effect with fixed fan-out. The read-then-decrement is not atomic: a latent defect, not a vocabulary gap.

title: Summarize different types of files (S3 event, ingest by type, summarize)

gaps.fragment: Choices: Variable $.detail.object.key StringMatches '*txt' | '*pdf' | '*docx', Default: UnsupportedFileType (Type: Fail)
gaps.why: a router by kind decided by a code string match, with an explicit unsupported branch that fails; P07 shape with the none option present

note: An S3 object event (the input is an EventBridge detail), a Choice on the file extension to one of three ingest functions, then one summarise function (the model call is inside the Lambda; the definition names it Summarize) and a Fail for other types. Route by kind in code, ingest, summarise.

title: Batch job with a pre-processing lambda

gaps.fragment: Resource: arn:aws:states:::batch:submitJob.sync, TimeoutSeconds: 3600
gaps.why: start a job and wait until it completes (the .sync integration); a bounded wait for an external completion, L0 wait.signal (19, N) or poll-until-ready (P21) with the 3,600 s timeout as its literal cap

note: Two states: a Lambda builds the job input, then a Batch job is submitted and awaited. Linear chain plus a bounded wait.

title: Gather and save resource configuration data (paginated, nested map)

gaps.fragment: Choice $.NextToken IsPresent -> ListAggregateDiscoveredResources-Pagination -> MapResolverRulesAndAssociations -> Choice (a cycle with no counter)
gaps.why: pagination as a state cycle with no page cap; L0 refuses an unbounded loop, pagination is an L3 capability with maxPages, so the rewrite is a bounded for with a cap

gaps.fragment: Retry: MaxAttempts 20, BackoffRate 2, IntervalSeconds 5 (States.Timeout, States.TaskFailed)
gaps.why: retry with a literal attempt cap, covered by L0 retry (20); the backoff grows to days, a defect of the definition, not a gap

note: Nested INLINE maps: for each resource type, list discovered resources (paginated) then for each resource batch-get the configuration and write it to S3 under a name-or-id key chosen by a Choice. Nested map, pagination, per-effect retry, S3 writes (a backup sync).

title: Serverless web contact form processor

gaps.fragment: Type: Pass, Parameters: { 'ticketId.$': 'States.UUID()' }
gaps.why: a random ticket id minted in a pure transform; randomness is not a field of step (see the inventory item)

note: A form message is scored for sentiment by a managed NLP service (a typed read, judge or an L3 tool), recorded in DynamoDB with retry and backoff, then a Choice on NEGATIVE publishes to SNS, otherwise succeeds. The default branch routes unknown sentiment as positive (a silent default, a defect).

title: Notification on an AWS Batch job completion

gaps.fragment: Resource: arn:aws:states:::batch:submitJob.sync, TimeoutSeconds: 3600
gaps.why: submit and await completion, bounded by a literal timeout (L0 wait.signal or P21)

note: Submit a Batch job and wait; Retry on any error (2 attempts, 30 s, backoff 1.5); Catch routes any error to a failure notification and success routes to a success notification (SNS).

title: Text processing for each SQS message (Express workflow)
note: One workflow run per queue message (the title and Comment say so; the trigger is outside the definition): decode base64, compute statistics, strip special characters, tokenize and count, four Lambda invocations in a row.

title: AWS Support case notifications
note: An event carrying a case id: fetch the case (SDK integration), Choice on severity critical or urgent publishes an SNS message built with States.Format, otherwise Succeed.

title: ATM dispenser as a chain of responsibility
note: Four Lambda tasks in sequence (Dispense50, 20, 10, 1), each with Retry (3 attempts, 2 s, backoff 2) on one error name. The chain-of-responsibility semantics (each handler takes what it can and passes the remainder) is inside the Lambdas, not in the definition.

title: Lookout for Vision inference (check model, start, wait, infer, copy anomalies)

gaps.fragment: Check Model Status -> Model Ready? -> Wait 30 second -> Check Model Status (default and STARTING_HOSTING loop back with no counter)
gaps.why: poll until the model is HOSTED, a cycle with no attempt cap and no timeout; P21 poll until ready needs a literal cap, so the rewrite adds a bounded for and a timeout guard

note: Check a vision model's status; TRAINED starts it and waits 30 s, STARTING_HOSTING and any other status wait 30 s and re-check, HOSTED runs an inference Lambda (retry with backoff on service errors) and a Choice on anomalous copies the object to a result bucket, else succeeds. A state machine over model status.
